notes.whyTheseNumbersChanged: v1's five numbers were round aspirations (250 KB / 416 KB / 300 KB / 1150 KB) written as a gate and never run: no CI job executed check-bundle.mjs, and measured against HEAD on 2026-08-23 THREE of the five failed — entry 287,644 > 256,000, initial 482,196 > 425,984, total 1,273,275 > 1,177,600. A budget nobody ran is not a budget. v2 replaces the wishes with a RATCHET: each ceiling is the measured value of a green build plus a stated margin, so a regression is caught on the day it lands instead of being invisible behind a number that was already red. The aspiration is not thrown away — it is kept below, as `target`, which is where it belonged all along.
notes.margin: ~5% over measured, on every byte ceiling. Wide enough that ordinary feature work does not churn this file; far tighter than the 76,736-byte regression that returning the dev MockCore to the entry chunk would cause, which the v1 ceilings would have accepted in silence.

target.owed: Total JS is 32,746 bytes over the standing aspiration and cannot be closed by splitting: `vendor-support` (256,274 bytes) is lodash + ajv + d3, pulled in transitively by @jsonforms and @xyflow, and NONE of it is on the startup path. Closing it means changing one of those two dependencies, which is a decision, not a chore. Tracked in progress.md Now/Next; the gate that closes it is a build measuring under 1,177,600 with the required splits intact.

notes.whyTheseNumbersChangedAgain: 2026-08-26: the entry ceiling was RE-BASELINED 174,000 -> 199,000, and the reason is written down because `notes.margin` says a ceiling raised without knowing which change spent the bytes is not a ceiling. It was red on HEAD before this session touched anything, and BISECTED rather than guessed: eleven commits built from clean detached checkouts, entry chunk measured by `stat` each time — 86df2ea 166,665 / ff5b73a 167,559 / e5f74ff 167,552 / 1ec9478 167,526 / b610775 167,535 / f5b5d19 168,044 / 6932aab 168,044 / 096be3a 168,044 / 4e845c5 168,769 / b2cd35e 168,769 / 58e181c 188,679. One commit, +19,910 bytes, straight through a 174,000 ceiling. `58e181c` landed `theme/icons.tsx` (878 lines, 161 inline-SVG drawings — 166 path literals costing 7,575 bytes in the entry alone), `theme/assets.tsx` and `theme/timeline.tsx` as NEW files; `icons.tsx` and `assets.tsx` are reachable from first paint because the Engines rail, the header, the hierarchy and the empty state all draw marks before anything else loads. That is `first-paint.json`'s counter-rule exactly: a surface whose job is to be there when you first look cannot be the one that loads last, and an icon that pops in after the chunk arrives is the ADR-131 blank-control defect arriving late instead of never. So the bytes are DELIBERATE and the stale number is the defect. The new ceiling is a measured green build (189,845, this tree, after ADR-147 moved the settings-sheet family out of the entry) plus the same ~5% margin. ADR-147's own contribution is 1,166 bytes of that, measured against 58e181c's 188,679. The INITIAL ceiling moves with it and for the same reason, not as a second judgement: initial = the entry plus the two chunks it statically imports (vendor-react, vendor-state), so every byte of the entry is also an initial byte. HEAD measured 383,231 against 378,000 — red on its own, before this session — and this tree measures 384,397. Both new ceilings are a measured green build plus ~5%. The other three were and remain green at both points: largest 256,274 <= 270,000, total 1,267,741 <= 1,272,000, 33 chunks >= 24.

notes.whyTheEntryChangedAgain: 2026-08-28 (ADR-171): the ENTRY ceiling was RE-BASELINED 199,000 -> 210,000, measured as a clean A/B rather than guessed, because `notes.margin` says a ceiling raised without knowing which change spent the bytes is not a ceiling. Two production `vite build`s minutes apart against one `node_modules`: HEAD (`7a22382`) in a detached worktree measures entry 194,289 / initial 388,841 / largest 256,274 / total 1,297,496 across 36 chunks; this tree measures entry 200,567. The +6,278 bytes are aiming a shot by pointing at it: the aim session store (shared by the bottom dock, which starts the mode, and the shell, which lives it), the hover-settle read on the viewport's own handler, and `SubjectAimBadge` — the only thing on screen saying a click now aims instead of selects. MEASURED THE OTHER WAY TOO: deferring the badge alone lands the entry at 198,708, which is 292 bytes under the old ceiling and would be spent by the next edit — and it buys a mode badge that can arrive a frame after the mode it announces, which is `first-paint.json`'s counter-rule in miniature. The bytes are deliberate; the stale number is the defect. New ceiling = this measured green build plus the same ~5% margin every other ceiling here carries. THE OTHER FOUR DO NOT MOVE, and that is the check on this one: initial is 395,119 against 403,000 (every entry byte is also an initial byte, so it rose by exactly the same 6,278 and still fits), largest is unchanged at 256,274 <= 270,000, total 1,304,801 <= 1,351,000, and the chunk count is unchanged at 36 >= 24.
notes.whyTheTotalChangedAgain2026_08_28: The TOTAL ceiling was re-baselined 1,272,000 -> 1,278,000, and — per `notes.margin`, which says a ceiling raised without knowing which change spent the bytes is not a ceiling — the bytes are named rather than waved through. MEASURED, not guessed: a clean detached worktree at the base commit 1bcdc89, production `vite build`, TOTAL 1,271,877 in 33 chunks. So the ceiling had 123 bytes of headroom left BEFORE this session touched anything: it was set on 2026-08-26 against a measured 1,267,741 and the lanes that landed between then and 1bcdc89 spent 4,136 of the 4,259 it allowed. This tree measures 1,273,856 in 34 chunks — +1,979 bytes, and every one of them is accounted for: `SwatchGrid`/`SwatchTile` (the picker form of a tile, adopted byte-identically from the material-picker lane), the `AssetChip` action form, six landform path tables for the terrain presets, and eleven `disabledReason` sentences that R9 requires and that eleven controls in TerrainPanel did not have. Where they went: TerrainPanel's own lazy chunk 27,559 -> 28,583 (+1,024), the entry 190,046 -> 190,067 (+21 — the terrain surface is not startup work and did not become it), and a NEW `assets-*` chunk holding `theme/assets.tsx`, which Vite hoisted the moment a second lazy panel imported it. That last one is the shared-component split working: the tile family is now downloaded once for the asset library and the terrain picker rather than twice. The new ceiling is this measured build plus 4,144 bytes — the same ~0.33% the total ceiling has carried since v2, deliberately tighter than the ~5% the other four get, because `target.totalJavaScriptBytes` is still owed.
